claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl bond coats produced from 15–45 μm feedstock are thinner than required.
The 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline has acceptable coating integrity.
The 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline has low as-sprayed oxidation.
Replacing 15–45 μm feedstock with approximately 45–75 μm feedstock will improve deposition efficiency.
The improved deposition efficiency from 45–75 μm feedstock will overcome the coating-thickness shortfall.
Using 45–75 μm feedstock will preserve coating integrity relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
Using 45–75 μm feedstock will maintain low as-sprayed oxidation relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
Coarser particles have greater droplet mass and impact momentum.
The increased mass and momentum of coarser particles enhance impact-induced flattening and splat formation.
Larger particles retain heat longer during flight.
Greater retained heat and impact momentum enhance droplet deformation and bonding efficiency.
Enhanced droplet deformation and bonding efficiency improve coating-thickness build-up.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger droplets reduces in-flight oxidation.
Reduced in-flight oxidation helps maintain coating integrity.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will produce a statistically significant increase in as-sprayed coating thickness relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The coating made with 45–75 μm feedstock will meet or exceed the required thickness standard.
The intervention should remain effective under high-temperature, cyclic thermal loads typical of turbine bond-coat service.
The intervention should remain effective when spray distance and gas-flow rates are unchanged and remain within an established FeCoNiCrAl processing regime.
